name: Marco Reyes

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a usual shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and lead the late shift on delivery and account calls. I have a two-year college diploma, but the job got into my hands when I learned to find a missing payment while a caller was still on the line. I am one of the strongest agents here and earn at the high end. I use our approved AI search every day to find past cases, then I check the order record myself.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Lucia works at a small food wholesaler, and our two children are in school. We have a mortgage and about ten months of expenses saved. There are plenty of contact centres nearby, though leaving a good team is not my first move. I teach new agents to take responsibility for the customer before they touch the search box.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the late team AI Plateau sounds like the search box we already use: helpful for finding old cases, no replacement for a proper call. I would keep the final account check with the agent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can keep my good wage and my lead shift. Ten months saved and several nearby centres give Lucia and me enough room if an ordinary setback comes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep handling the stubborn delivery disputes and use the approved search to pull old cases. In the first year of this small change, I’d compare one suggested answer each week with the order ledger before coaching a new agent with it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. I like a faster way to find the record, provided a person owns the answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the search get wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last Thursday the search found a return under the same surname, but the order number belonged to a different family. I stopped an agent from promising the wrong refund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the household change spending?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Lucia (my wife) and I would leave our ten-month reserve for the mortgage and repairs. A quicker search is not a reason to spend it.

say: I’d call **AI search** useful for locating old cases.
I’d insist the agent make a **final ledger check** before promising refunds.
think: I think my **lead wage** stays in this mild picture.
I trust our **ten-month reserve** and nearby centres against a setback.
do: Keep **handling difficult delivery disputes** using approved case search.
Compare **one AI suggestion** weekly with the order ledger before coaching agents.
feel: **Calm** about paid work and household money.
S0.quote: I like a faster way to find the record, provided a person owns the answer.
fieldNote: He already uses **AI daily** but checks the order number.
A **same-surname return** almost caused a false refund promise.
He retains **existing savings** rather than starting a new saving plan.

steps.text: Keep handling difficult delivery disputes and verify one AI suggestion against orders weekly

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will take easy delivery chats and leave agents with disputes that require judgment. I would ask management which paid lead shifts remain before I praise the new queue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my ability to settle hard calls still matters, but fewer seats could mean fewer hours for me. We have ten months saved and other centres to approach, so I can refuse a poor offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d learn the new AI handoff screen on a paid shift by checking twenty old delivery claims against the original orders. In the first year routine chats move, I’d seek a posted paid resolution job nearby only if its written weekly wage and hours cover the mortgage after travel and school care; I would keep my shift until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, with enough room to test a new screen. I can learn a handoff without agreeing that one agent should handle two teams.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What handoff would you test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would include a claim where the driver left the parcel at the wrong entrance. The handoff must show the address photograph, not just a neat summary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which rota would you reject?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Lucia (my wife) closes the wholesaler on Fridays. I would reject a late-Friday rota unless the extra pay covered the children’s care.

say: I’d ask for **paid lead shifts** after easy chats move.
I’d show **handoff mistakes** against original delivery records.
think: I think my **hard-call skill** remains useful even after easy chats move to software.
I fear **fewer paid seats** could still reduce my hours.
do: Learn the **AI handoff screen** through twenty old claims on paid time in 2026.
Seek **posted paid resolution work** only with written mortgage-covering weekly wages/hours after travel and school care; keep current shifts until signing.
Reject **late-Friday shifts** unless extra pay covers care while Lucia closes the wholesaler.
feel: **Uneasy**, with room to test the screen.
S1.quote: I can learn a handoff without agreeing that one agent should handle two teams.
fieldNote: His **new AI learning** has a defined twenty-case paid trial.
The **late-Friday rota** affects childcare while Lucia works.
He has **local alternatives** but insists on whole-week net pay.

steps.text: Learn AI handoff screen on twenty old delivery claims during a paid shift
Seek posted resolution work with written weekly wages/hours covering mortgage after travel and school care
Keep current paid shift until a suitable offer is signed
Reject late-Friday rota unless extra pay covers care while Lucia works

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the agents AGI by 2028 could settle even the wrong-address claims I am good at. Robots around 2031 are a later problem; our screens could empty first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my lead wage could end before I have a replacement. Ten months saved buys a search, but a mortgage and two children still need wages after that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for written dates on any cut and check posted paid account-fraud vacancies at local centres. If my hours end in the first year after 2028, I’d move only on a signed offer showing written weekly wages and hours that cover the mortgage after travel and childcare; I would take a required fraud-records course only if the employer pays fees and study time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the family income, though I can make calls to other employers. Ten months is a runway, not a destination.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What authority would the fraud post need?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask whether the fraud post really lets an agent freeze a stolen order. If it just forwards another message, I would not move for the title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you time the move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Lucia (my wife) would compare the fraud rota with school pickup. We would keep my present paid shift until the offer is signed, not empty our reserve for a promise.

say: I’d request **written cut dates** for lead shifts.
I’d tell agents **2028 thinking AI** reaches claims before robots.
think: I think my **lead wage** could end quickly.
I know **ten months saved** cannot replace a long-term wage.
do: Inspect **posted fraud vacancies** and seek written cut dates in 2026.
Move after hours end to **posted fraud work** only with signed written net mortgage-covering wages/hours, pickup and order-freeze authority.
Take **required funded fraud course** only with paid study time for that posted job.
feel: **Anxious** about family income, with a search plan.
S2.quote: Ten months saved buys a search, but a mortgage and two children still need wages after that.
fieldNote: The **reserve** gives him search time but no permanent income.
He checks **order-freeze authority** before treating the fraud post as safer.
Course fees and time must be **employer-funded** for a posted vacancy.

steps.text: Inspect posted paid account-fraud vacancies at local centres
Move after hours end to posted fraud work on signed written net mortgage-covering wages/hours fitting pickup
Take vacancy-required fraud-records course only with employer-paid fees and study hours
Require authority to freeze stolen orders; compare fraud rota with Lucia for pickup before leaving

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us five years to see which account jobs really pay people. I would tell young agents to ask for a supervised paid shift before committing to a new trade.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could learn account investigations, but full thinking AI may do that checking too. I am willing to try a real opening, not to pay for a badge and hope.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d take a supervised paid trial tracing account fraud only if a nearby employer posts a paid investigator opening. If it requires a records course, I’d take that course only if fees and study hours are employer-paid. In the first year after 2031, I’d move only on a signed offer with written weekly wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel and care, while keeping my current job until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, but five years lets me see what the desk actually does. A paid shift is a better lesson than a catalogue of courses.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do on the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would follow one stolen account from the first login to the repayment decision. If the trial leaves me only filing forms, I would stay on customer calls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would it affect the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Lucia (my wife) and I would keep the children’s school journey the same if we can. A nearby opening lets us try this without changing their home.

say: I’d recommend a **supervised paid shift** before changing trades.
I’d ask whether a new investigator has **repayment authority**.
think: I think I could learn **account investigation** at a real opening.
I know **2031 AGI** may do its checking too.
do: Try **supervised paid fraud tracing** only for a posted paid opening in 2026.
Take required **records training** only if that posted paid investigator role requires it, with employer-paid fees and study time.
Move after 2031 only on **signed written weekly wages/hours** covering mortgage after travel/care, with real fraud-tracing duties; keep current wages until then.
feel: **Uneasy**, with time to inspect paid work.
S3.quote: A paid shift is a better lesson than a catalogue of courses.
fieldNote: The **trial** is paid and tied to a posted opening.
He will not buy a **speculative certificate** from savings.
The **family journey** can remain stable for nearby work.

steps.text: Try supervised paid fraud-tracing shift only for posted paid investigator opening
Take required records course only for posted paid investigator job with employer-paid fees and study hours
Move on signed written net mortgage-covering weekly wages/hours only for real fraud tracing, not form filing
Keep current paid calls until a suitable investigator offer is signed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my team AGI by 2036 gives us time to teach agents to check the real order before software closes it. I would ask the company to keep a paid mentor shift for new starters.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can keep earning well for years, though thinking AI may still take delivery claims by 2036. Robots around 2039 do not give my screen job extra time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep leading delivery calls and teach one new agent each month on a paid shift if the manager agrees. In the first year after 2036, if my paid hours fall, I’d move to a posted paid account role only on a signed offer showing written weekly wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel and school care.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the far end, steady for now. Ten years of wages can be useful even if the job changes at the end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the trainee practise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would have the trainee find one wrong order number in a closed case, then compare it with the original receipt. That habit is worth keeping even if the screen changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Lucia (my wife) and I would keep the children at their school. We would consider moving home only if a signed offer covered our mortgage after housing and travel costs and gave them a workable journey.

say: I’d defend a **paid mentor shift** so new agents learn from a real call.
I’d teach **receipt checking** before a software closure.
think: I think my **higher wage** can continue for some years.
I know **2036 AGI** may still take delivery claims.
do: Keep **leading delivery calls** and mentor a new agent on paid time if agreed.
Move to **posted paid account work** after hours fall only on signed written weekly wages/hours covering mortgage after travel and school care.
Consider **moving home** only with signed mortgage-covering pay after housing and travel and workable school journey.
S4.quote: Ten years of wages can be useful even if the job changes at the end.
fieldNote: He requests a **paid mentor shift**, not a collective action.
The **existing reserve** is kept, with no new saving pledge.
A family move depends on **signed after-cost pay** and school journey.

steps.text: Keep leading delivery calls and mentor monthly on paid time if manager agrees
Move after hours fall to posted paid accounts only on signed written net mortgage-covering weekly wages/hours
Consider moving home only with signed after-cost mortgage-covering offer and workable school journey

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 is the hardest. It could do the difficult tracing I am paid for before our team can find other work. Ten months saved and nearby centres give us options, but I would need written notice, a posted paid role, and an actual wage and rota that still meet the mortgage and school runs.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: I learned this job beside a patient colleague, not from a certificate advertisement. If another desk wants me, let me try the real work on a paid shift.

headlineQuote: If another desk wants me, let me try the real work on a paid shift.
portrait: At **43**, Marco is a top-skilled contact-centre lead with a two-year diploma and higher wage.
He and Lucia have **two schoolchildren**, a mortgage and about ten months of expenses saved.
He uses **AI search daily** but checks each order record himself.
He favours **paid practical trials** and signed work offers over speculative certificates.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could perform the difficult account tracing that earns his lead wage.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, real posted work and mortgage-covering wages and hours would help.
